articles.title: Riverton's Kestrel Bridge to close for three weeks for repairs
articles.description: Riverton's Kestrel Bridge will shut for three weeks over the summer holidays so crews can resurface both approaches and reseal the deck.
articles.content:
Riverton's Kestrel Bridge will close to all traffic for three weeks during the summer holidays while crews carry out overdue repairs.
The city council said the work would include resurfacing the southern approach, replacing expansion joints and resealing the steel deck.
Buses will be diverted over the Millrace crossing, and extra ferry services will run between the two river banks.
Council works director Imogen Tarrant said the timing had been chosen because traffic usually falls by about a third over the break.
"Doing this in stages would stretch the disruption over most of the year," she said.
Cyclists and pedestrians will keep access to the eastern footpath for most of the closure.
Local traders on Quayside Road have asked for parking fees to be waived while the bridge is shut.
The council said it would review the request but warned that a temporary toll on the Millrace crossing would only be used as a "last resort".

articles.title: Prediction: What a $5,000 Stake in Corvane Semiconductor Could Be Worth by 2030
articles.description: Can the chip designer keep growing at this pace, or is the rally running out of steam?
articles.content:
Corvane Semiconductor has been one of the strongest performers among mid-sized chip designers this year.
The company sells processors for data centers, gaming consoles and industrial robots.
Its data center unit now brings in more than half of total revenue, up from about a third two years ago.
Management expects that share to keep rising as cloud providers build out new computing clusters.
Key numbers
Revenue last quarter grew 31% from a year earlier.
Gross margin widened by two percentage points.
The company ended the quarter with more cash than debt.
What could go wrong
Corvane competes with much larger rivals that can spend more on research.
A slowdown in cloud spending would hit its fastest-growing business first.
The stock also trades at a premium to the sector, which leaves little room for disappointment.
Should you buy now?
If revenue keeps compounding at even half its recent pace, a $5,000 stake could be worth considerably more by 2030.
Long-term investors who can live with volatility may want to start with a small position and add over time.

articles.title: Halden Electronics eyes record quarterly profit as memory margins widen
articles.description: Halden Electronics is expected to report its highest quarterly operating profit ever, with memory chip margins seen above 70 percent.
articles.content:
Halden Electronics is on track to post a record operating profit for the third quarter, according to analyst estimates compiled on Sunday.
Brokerages expect the company's memory division to account for most of the gain as contract prices for server memory keep climbing.
Margins on dynamic memory are estimated at more than 70 percent, the widest in the company's history.
Demand from data center operators has outpaced new production capacity for three straight quarters.
Halden has said it will add two production lines at its Varn Valley campus next year.
Its smartphone and display units are expected to report flat results.
"Memory supply will stay tight into next year, and that keeps pushing prices higher," said Theo Brandt, an analyst at Northfield Securities.
The company will publish preliminary results in early October.
